segments.text: Rebels reached the presidential palace in the centre of the capital.

Séléka leader Michel Djotodia, who served after the January agreement as First Deputy Prime Minister for National Defense, declared himself President, becoming the first Muslim to hold the office. Djotodia said that there would be a three-year transitional period and that Nicolas Tiangaye would continue to serve as Prime Minister.
Séléka forces moved to western part of CAR, capturing Paoua, Bouar and Nola
FDPC withdrew from Séléka coalition. In response, Séléka launched heavy attack on FDPC positions near Baboua, killing some fighters.
LRA established their base in Fodé in Mbomou.
Anti-balaka attacked Zéré on the road between Bouca and Bossangoa, killing at least 55 civilians.
Anti-balaka attacked Seleka in Bouca.

segments.text: 3R took control of Koundjili in Ouham-Pende. Local population fled to bush.
Prefect of Nana-Grébizi prefecture fled his residence in Kaga-Bandoro after demonstrators accused him of collaborating with MPC rebels in city. They ransacked his residence.
3R attacked USMS base in Wantiguira, located 8 km from Bouar with heavy weapons.
Anti-balaka in Bozoum held a meeting demanding resignation of Ouham-Pende prefect accusing him of collaborating with 3R rebels.
MPC took control of Boguila, Nana-Bakassa and Beboura following MINUSCA withdrawal
Bangladeshi paratroopers from MINUSCA attacked 3R in Koui.
Demonstrators burned down police headquarters in Bagandou after police killed ex-Anti-balaka commander.
Police forces from Bangui were sent to Bagandou to restore peace, however they were stopped by a crowd.
A UN peacekeeper was killed and two others wounded in an ambush set up by the 3R militia.
3R forces attacked Ngbama village near Bocaranga kidnapping 40 people and stealing 50 million CFA francs.
MINUSCA forces recaptured Niem from 3R forces.

segments.text: Janjaweed militias attacked village near Am Dafock killing more than 140 people and displacing thousands.
Anti-balaka attacked Grimari blocking roads to Sibut and Bambari. FACA managed to recapture city the same day killing one Anti-balaka commander.
FACA captured Koui after battle with 3R.
Local militias took control of Gaga town near Yaloké after clashes with FACA soldiers. They ransacked buildings of Chinese companies operating in the area.

Three armed Anti-balaka fighters from Gaga raided home of brigade commander of Yaloké's gendarmerie and forced him to free one of their fighters who was arrested for looting. Local population organizer a protest against his decision.
3R briefly captured Bohong and Mbotoga before withdrawing later that day. Local population fled to bush.
3R captured four villages (Yambassa, Bavara, Bondja and Bimbi) near Paoua. They withdrew day later, but returned on 19 September.
MINUSCA and FACA forces were sent to recapture Bavara from 3R but were forced to withdraw after their vehicles were unable to cross a bridge.
3R took control of Nanga-Boguila.

In response, self-defense forces from South Sudan attacked Bambouti, kicking UPC out of the city and killing some of their fighters. They withdrew a few hours later. UPC militants kidnapped the local mayor after returning to Bambouti.

segments.text: Sudanese Arab militias attacked Boromata village. They were repulsed by Goula militias. A few people were killed.

Clashes erupted between FACA and UPC rebels in Bambari resulting in a few rebels being killed.

segments.text: Anti-balaka attacked Yaloké and Bossembélé. Yaloké was captured by rebels and four soldiers were killed. Bossembélé was also reportedly captured by rebels. Reinforcement was sent from Bangui to recapture Bossembélé. Boda and Mbaiki were also reportedly captured by rebels.
MINUSCA was deployed in rebel-held Bossembélé and Bossemptele to restore peace. Gallo was captured by rebels. Heavy clashes erupted in Mbaiki between rebels and FACA supported by Russian mercenaries.

segments.text: Armed forces reportedly destroyed rebel base 1 km from place where massacre near Bossangoa happened.

Russian forces using four helicopters attacked 3R positions west of Koui killing three people.
Heavy clashes were ongoing between Russian mercenaries and 3R rebels in Sabewa, Bozou and other villages. At least one rebel and Russian soldier were killed. Three Russian vehicles were torched.
3R rebels kidnapped three people on the outskirts of Bozoum.
Two motorcycle drivers were killed by mine explosions in Ouham-Pende.
Around 50 3R rebels attacked Dilapoko village killing one person.
3R rebels occupied Zoukombo village on Beloko-Baboua road. They withdrew later that day.

Two soldiers were killed and two kidnapped in UPC attack on Kombele village near Bambari.

Russian mercenaries attacked UPC positions near Ngakobo, in Pouloubou and Kolo. In Nagkobo, 13 civilians were killed. In Pouloubou 19 civilians and 6 UPC rebels were killed and a UPC general was injured. In Kolo an estimated 42 people were killed.

On November 13, 2006, a third town in northern CAR, Sam Ouandja, was seized by the UFDR.
The FDPC's Abdoulaye Miskine signed a peace agreement with the government on 2 February 2007 in Syrte.
After French Mirage jets bombed the UFDR headquarters in Birao, the UFDR and the CAR government signed the Birao Peace Agreement on 1 April 2007.
On 9 May 2008 the APRD signed a cease fire and peace agreement with the government in Libreville.
On 21 June 2008 the FDPC joined the APRD and UFDR in signing the Libreville Comprehensive Peace Agreement, which reiterated and extended the provisions of the previous two agreements.
The most important agreement, the Global Peace Accord (signed in Libreville, Gabon, on 21 June 2008), was first signed by the ARPD, UFDR, and FDPC groups.
On 25 August 2008 the CPJP finally acceded to the Libreville comprehensive agreement.
The only major group not to sign an agreement at the time was the CPJP, which continued its activities and signed a peace agreement with the government on 25 August 2012.
On 10 December 2012, the conflict restarted with rebel groups accusing President Bozizé of violating the terms of their earlier agreement.
The new rebel coalition, known as Séléka, overthrew Bozizé and took the capital, Bangui, on 24 March 2013, and rebel leader Michel Djotodia declared himself President of the Central African Republic.
